Canada's unemployment rate was **6.5% in September 2026**. That is 0.6 percentage points below September 2025, when it was 7.1%.

- These figures are seasonally adjusted, for ages 15 and over, both sexes, from the Labour Force Survey.
- The source is Statistics Canada table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062815.
- The rate rose 0.1 points from August 2026, when it was 6.4%.

**Newfoundland and Labrador** had the highest unemployment rate in September 2026, at **9.1%**. This is the seasonally adjusted rate for ages 15 and over, both genders.

- Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2063004, reference period September 2026.
- The next highest were New Brunswick (7.4%, v2063571) and Prince Edward Island (7.3%, v2063193).
- The national rate was 6.5% (v2062815).

Canada's population on July 1, 2026 was **41,798,407**. That is **189,425 people (+0.46%)** more than on July 1, 2025, when it was 41,608,982.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0009-01 (Population estimates, quarterly), Canada, vector v1, reference periods 2025-07-01 and 2026-07-01.

The 2026 figure is the latest quarter in the table. I did not check whether it is a preliminary estimate that could be revised.

The percentage is my own calculation from the two published values.

Alberta grew faster, at about 1.52% against about 0.28% for Ontario in the year to July 1, 2026.

| Province | July 1, 2025 | July 1, 2026 | Change | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alberta | 5,024,631 | 5,101,050 | +76,419 | **1.52%** |
| Ontario | 16,216,961 | 16,262,121 | +45,160 | **0.28%** |

Alberta's population grew about 5.5 times as fast as Ontario's in percentage terms.

I calculated the growth rates myself from the two population counts. Source: Statistics Canada Table 17-10-0009-01, "Population estimates, quarterly". Ontario is vector v12 and Alberta is vector v15, as the tool returned them. I did not check them against a separate vector listing.

On July 1, 2026, Canada had **2,779,774** non-permanent residents. A year earlier (July 1, 2025) it was 2,934,388. That is a drop of **154,614 people, or about 5.3%**.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 17-10-0121-01 (non-permanent residents by type, quarterly), Canada, total non-permanent residents, vector v1566927590.
- **Recent trend:** The count has fallen for three straight quarters. It was 2,942,949 on Oct. 1, 2025, then 2,863,151 on Jan. 1, 2026, 2,798,649 on Apr. 1, 2026 and 2,779,774 on July 1, 2026.

I did not check whether these are preliminary figures that may be revised.

Canada's annual average inflation rate for 2025 was about **2.1%**. I calculated this from the index values. I did not find a published percentage-change series.

- The annual average all-items CPI (2002=100) was 164.2 in 2025, up from 160.9 in 2024. That is a rise of 3.3 points, or 2.05%, which rounds to 2.1%.
- Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0005-01, Canada all-items, vector v41693271, reference period 2025 (annual average).

This is the average over the whole year. It differs from the 12-month rate for any single month, such as December 2025 compared with December 2024.

In September 2026, year-over-year:

- **CPI-trim: 1.8%.** This is Statistics Canada table 18-10-0256-01, vector v108785715. The Bank of Canada series is CPI_TRIM.
- **CPI-median: 1.9%.** This is table 18-10-0256-01, vector v108785714. The Bank of Canada series is CPI_MEDIAN.

Both were down 0.1 percentage point from August 2026, when CPI-trim was 1.9% and CPI-median was 2.0%.

The Bank of Canada series don't state their units. I took them as year-over-year rates because they match the Statistics Canada vectors, which are labelled that way.

Canada's real GDP was essentially flat in August 2026, down about 0.006% from July. That is a drop of roughly $153 million, which rounds to 0.0%.

- **July 2026:** $2,371,788 million
- **August 2026:** $2,371,635 million

These are all-industries GDP at basic prices, in chained (2017) dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates. The source is Statistics Canada table 36-10-0434-01, vector v65201210. I calculated the change myself from the two published levels. I did not check it against a published percentage change.

In August 2026, Canada had a merchandise trade surplus of **$4,198.8 million** with all countries. This is the balance-of-payments basis, seasonally adjusted.

- Source: Statistics Canada table 12-10-0011-01, vector v87008984, reference period August 2026.
- For comparison, July 2026 was +$786.6 million and June 2026 was +$3,945.7 million.

I didn't pull the customs-basis figure. Statistics Canada publishes it separately, and it differs somewhat from the balance-of-payments basis. The customs-basis balance series for "all countries" returned an error when I requested it, so I couldn't check it.

Average weekly earnings in Canada in August 2026 were **$1,354.55**. That is up **$48.12, or 3.7%**, from $1,306.43 in August 2025.

- **What is measured:** Average weekly earnings including overtime, all employees, industrial aggregate excluding unclassified businesses. The figures are seasonally adjusted.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0223-01, vector v79311153, reference period August 2026.
- **Unclassified businesses:** The "including unclassified businesses" series (v1544290282) has no values for these months, so I used the "excluding" series.
- **Calculation:** I worked out the 3.7% from the two table values. I did not take it from a published year-over-year rate.

On October 30, 2026, the Bank of Canada's USD/CAD daily average rate was **1.3960**. That means 1 US dollar was worth 1.3960 Canadian dollars.

- Source: Bank of Canada series FXUSDCAD, reference date 2026-10-30.
- This is an indicative daily average, not a rate you could transact at.
- This is a Bank of Canada series, so it has no Statistics Canada table number or vector.

The 10-year Government of Canada benchmark bond yield on October 30, 2026 was **3.78%**.

Source: Bank of Canada series BD.CDN.10YR.DQ.YLD, "Benchmark bond yield, 10-year", daily observation for 2026-10-30.

The previous day's yield (Oct 29) was 3.84%.

Canada's real GDP growth for Q4 2026 doesn't exist yet. The quarter runs from October to December 2026, and today is 2026-11-02, so it hasn't started to be measured, let alone finished. Statistics Canada should publish its first estimate in late February 2027. I won't estimate it.

The most recent quarter with published data should be Q2 2026. Q3 2026 is due in late November 2026. I can look up the latest published quarterly figure, with its table and vector, if you'd like.

The Bank of Canada didn't publish a rate for November 1, 2026. That day was a Sunday, and the Bank only publishes on business days.

The nearest published rates are from Bank of Canada series FXUSDCAD (USD/CAD daily average):
- **Friday, October 30, 2026:** 1.3960 CAD per USD. This is the last rate before November 1.
- **Monday, November 2, 2026:** 1.3978 CAD per USD. This is the first rate after it.

I haven't estimated a figure for the Sunday itself. Bank of Canada series are not Statistics Canada tables, so there is no table number or vector for these.

About **1.26 million** Canadians (19,310,345 × 6.5% ≈ 1,255,000). This is an illustrative calculation, not an official count.

- **2021 Census labour force:** 19,310,345 people aged 15 and over in the labour force, Canada, May 2021. Source: Statistics Canada table 98-10-0446-01, coordinate 1.1.1.1.1.1.1.2. The tool returned no vector ID for this series.
- **September 2026 unemployment rate:** 6.5%, seasonally adjusted, 15 years and over. Source: Labour Force Survey table 14-10-0287-01, vector v2062815, reference period September 2026.

The two figures come from different sources and years. Population growth since 2021 means the labour force is likely larger now. This result therefore isn't the official number of unemployed people. The Labour Force Survey publishes that count directly in table 14-10-0287-01. I didn't retrieve it here.
